name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
notes: 24/7 phone, chat and text with advocates; safety planning; referrals Cited by Alameda, SF, Santa Clara county pages.
whenToUse: You want anonymous support or are not sure where to start. Works while a partner is nearby if you use chat or text.
channelNotes: Chat at thehotline.org; text START to 88788.

name: CalVCB (California Victim Compensation Board)
notes: Pays crime-related costs not covered elsewhere: relocation, mental health, medical, dental, home security. Apply online (EN/ES) or by paper; an advocate can help via victims.ca.gov/get-help. Relay: 711. No police report required: DV program letter, medical/mental-health records or a restraining order can be used. Fact sheet does not name transportation or emergency housing explicitly; confirm with CalVCB.
whenToUse: You want help paying for relocation, counseling or medical costs. Application can be started while partner is home, but keep any paperwork where it can't be found.
channelNotes: Apply online (English/Spanish); no police report needed.

name: California Safe at Home (Secretary of State)
notes: Substitute mailing address accepted by state/county/city agencies; confidential voter registration. Enroll by appointment with a designated Enrolling Agency (look-up on the SOS site). Email SafeAtHome@sos.ca.gov. Also (916) 653-6814. Duration/renewal terms not stated on the page; confirm with program.
whenToUse: You want your new address kept confidential.
channelNotes: Requires an appointment with an enrolling agency.

name: NNEDV Safety Net (technology safety)
notes: Guidance on stalkerware, location tracking, account security, evidence documentation. Page advises clearing browser history after visiting if your device is monitored.
whenToUse: You think your phone or accounts are being monitored.
channelNotes: Read on a safer device. Clear browser history afterward.

name: Asian Women's Shelter
notes: Emergency shelter for women and children. Coordinated-entry access point 415-926-3328 (Mon-Fri 9:30 am-4 pm, phone only). Call the crisis line to access shelter.
whenToUse: You need a safe place to stay.

constraints.population: Women and children; API community focus

name: La Casa de las Madres
notes: Emergency shelter (8-week program) for women, teens and children; male children/teens welcome. Call crisis line to access shelter.
whenToUse: You need emergency shelter or want to text an advocate.

children.note: Women, teens and children; male children and teens welcome.

name: St. Vincent de Paul - Riley Center
hours: Access point Mon-Fri 9 am-12 pm and 1-4:30 pm; crisis line 24/7
notes: Emergency shelter; coordinated-entry access point for survivors.
whenToUse: You need a safe place to stay.

name: San Francisco SafeHouse
hours: Access point Mon 1-7:30 pm; Tue-Fri 1-5 pm and 6-11:30 pm
notes: Transitional housing, rapid rehousing, emergency hotel vouchers. Two sf.gov pages agree: SafeHouse access point = 1089 Mission St; Riley Center = 1175 Howard St. An HSH flyer PDF parsed with the labels swapped, so phone-confirm the address before sending someone in person.
whenToUse: You need hotel vouchers, transitional or rapid rehousing. In person only; check hours first.

name: Raphael House
notes: Shelter for families and women in late pregnancy. Intake via Bayview Access Point 415-430-6320 or Central City Access Point 415-644-0504. Page does not say it is DV-only.
whenToUse: You need a safe place to stay.

children.note: Families and women in late pregnancy

whenToUse: You want to talk to an advocate about safety, options or a plan.

whenToUse: You want to talk to an advocate about safety, options or a plan.

whenToUse: You want to talk to an advocate about safety, options or a plan.

name: Love Never Fails
whenToUse: You want to talk to an advocate about safety, options or a plan.

name: SF Mayor's Office for Victims' Rights
notes: Navigation help. Leave voicemail with name, number, whether it is safe to call and when, language; they reply within 48 business hours if safe. Online form: sf.gov/get-help-if-you-are-a-victim-or-survivor-in-san-francisco/. info.ovwr@sf.gov
whenToUse: You want someone to help you navigate SF services without calling a hotline. Form works while partner is home.
channelNotes: Online form at sf.gov/get-help-if-you-are-a-victim-or-survivor-in-san-francisco/. Voicemail: say if it is safe to call back and when. Reply within 48 business hours.

name: Community United Against Violence (CUAV) - LGBTQ+
notes: Free, no citizenship requirement. Support groups, legal assistance, resource list. 415-333-4357 listed as appointment phone. Directory says NO dedicated crisis line. Verify directly before labeling 415-333-4357 as a hotline.
whenToUse: You are LGBTQ+ and want a community-specific advocate.

name: Bay Area Legal Aid - San Francisco
notes: Family law incl. restraining orders for low-income survivors.
whenToUse: You want a restraining order, custody help or immigration relief.

name: CORA - Community Overcoming Relationship Abuse
notes: County's dedicated IPV agency. Confidential Safe Houses (adults with minor children; no gender requirement), free Legal Line, family-law representation, supportive housing (subsidized up to 1-3 years), counseling, children's program. resources@corasupport.org. Referral gateway to the PHS Safe Pets Program.
whenToUse: You need a safe house, legal help or a plan in San Mateo County. Ask about pet placement.
channelNotes: Hotline 24/7. Email resources@corasupport.org is listed, but response time is unknown; use the hotline for urgent needs.

children.note: Safe House accepts adults with minor children; boys' age limit not stated.

pets.note: Pets can be placed up to 30 days via PHS Safe Pets Program with CORA referral (SMC residents). Pets in the Safe House itself: not stated.

constraints.population: Anyone experiencing intimate partner abuse, any gender

name: San Mateo County Family Justice Center
notes: DA-operated, multidisciplinary: DV, sexual assault, child/elder abuse, trafficking. Source is a May 14, 2025 launch announcement. Opening date, phone, hours NOT confirmed. Verify it is open before showing.
whenToUse: You want several services (advocate, legal, police/DA) in one place.

name: San Mateo Superior Court restraining-order help
notes: Family Law Facilitator LiveChat; Guide and File online questionnaire (efile: sanmateo.courts.ca.gov/ogf); DVRO e-filing accepted; forms at Redwood City clerk. Bay Area Legal Aid San Mateo (650) 358-0745 reviews DVRO forms. Court page gives no phone for FLF/clerk.
whenToUse: You want to prepare a restraining order online. Works while partner is home.
channelNotes: Family Law Facilitator LiveChat; Guide and File builds and e-files DVRO forms online; e-filing accepted for DV orders.

name: Next Door Solutions to Domestic Violence
notes: Emergency shelter (~19 people/night), housing solutions, support groups. Free. ADA accessible, LGBTQ friendly. If shelter is full, 'no one is turned away without an alternative housing solution'. Address conflict: county page says 234 E Gish Rd Ste 200, San Jose 95112; 1degree.org says 1400 Parkmoor Ave Ste 120, San Jose 95126. Confirm before directing anyone in person. Shelter info from 1degree (aggregator).
whenToUse: You need shelter in Santa Clara County; call to ask about space.

children.note: Boys and girls up to 18, and into adulthood when accompanying their mothers.

constraints.population: Women and their children; LGBTQ friendly

notes: Remote help via scscourt.org; phone (408) 882-2926. Prefer court's own flyer; call before travel.

channelNotes: Remote help through scscourt.org live chat and email; phone (408) 882-2926.

name: Text to 911 (San Mateo County)
notes: All county police, fire and sheriff dispatchers accept texts (since Oct 2018). Call if you can, text if you can't. English only. Needs a text/data plan and location services on. Give exact location; avoid emojis/abbreviations.
whenToUse: You are in immediate danger and cannot speak.
channelNotes: Silent option when you cannot speak. English only.

name: Text to 911 (Santa Clara County)
notes: Countywide since Sept 2019; texts route to the local jurisdiction's dispatcher. Dispatch cannot pinpoint location from a text; say where you are. 2019 news article: Los Gatos and Campbell were not yet live then; current status unconfirmed. Verify before publishing.
whenToUse: You are in immediate danger and cannot speak.
channelNotes: Silent option when you cannot speak.

name: Text to 911 (San Francisco)
notes: SF.gov's DV page says: if it isn't safe to call, you can text 911. Single-sentence official statement; details (languages, limits) not found.
whenToUse: You are in immediate danger and cannot speak.
channelNotes: Silent option when you cannot speak.

name: San Mateo County Victim Services Division
notes: Court support, emergency assistance, help with CalVCB application. Free; open to all regardless of immigration status, sexual orientation, gender identity, race, religion or income.
whenToUse: You want help with court, emergency aid or compensation.

citizenship_required.note: Open to all regardless of immigration status.

name: Rape Trauma Services (San Mateo County)
notes: 24-hr crisis line, accompaniment, advocacy, therapy; children, teens, families. Multiple languages. Free, no insurance needed. Sexual violence focus; include for survivors whose abuse includes sexual assault.
whenToUse: You want to talk to an advocate about safety, options or a plan.

name: Peninsula Humane Society & SPCA - Safe Pets Program
notes: Up to 30 days of free temporary housing for pets of DV victims. Must be a San Mateo County resident AND referred by CORA. Contact: Dayna Pesenti, dpesenti@phs-spca.org.
whenToUse: You are leaving and cannot take a pet to shelter. Ask CORA to refer you.
channelNotes: Referral comes through CORA; you do not contact PHS first. The PHS staff email is for advocates, not survivors.

pets.note: Up to 30 days, free; needs CORA referral and SMC residency.
